summary: Cross-team transfer: reconcile duplicated service accounts and equipment handover policy
description:
Issue summary: An engineer was transferred from Platform to Product as of 2026-03-01. HR flagged duplicate service accounts (two GitLab bot accounts and two AWS IAM users) and conflicting laptop assignment entries in inventory. Impact: potential privilege duplication and billing confusion for hardware loans; risk of orphaned keys.

Background: During the org swap HR changed manager and team tag in Workday which triggered automatic SCIM sync and contractor->employee provisioning flows in some cases. It appears the earlier contractor bot accounts were not deactivated before employee provisioning, plus there is an outstanding loaner laptop assigned under the contractor asset tag and a new company laptop provisioned.

Desired outcome: Remove/merge duplicate service accounts where appropriate, rotate any keys tied to the retired identity, ensure HR/IT inventory reflects single assigned device, and clarify policy and automation gap so future transfers don't leave duplicate identities. We need a short-term safe rollback plan and a longer-term policy/update to the SCIM/onboarding playbook.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) In Workday, change team tag from Platform to Product for a test user.
2) Observe SCIM provisioning events in Okta and GitLab within 5-20 minutes.
3) If user previously had a contractor bot/service account, check GitLab -> Admin -> Users for duplicate accounts with same email alias.
4) Check AWS IAM for duplicate users or access keys linked to both identities.
5) Check Asset Inventory (GOboard) for duplicate device assignments.
Expected: SCIM should consolidate or flag duplicates for manual review instead of creating separate active identical accounts.
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed two GitLab accounts: username liam.o (employee) and liam.o-contractor (legacy bot). Both share same email alias; contractor account still has two active PATs.
- AWS: Found IAM user liam-platform and liam-prod with overlapping policies; liam-platform has an access key last used 2026-02-28.
- Asset inventory: Loaner ID LO-4421 marked assigned to liam.o-contractor with status "in-use" and new laptop serial SN-7G4F assigned to liam.o with 'company-owned'. Shipping records show both devices were active simultaneously.
- SCIM logs (Okta export) show two provisioning events on 2026-03-01: one deprovision contract-role, one provision employee-role; webhook retries show a 409 conflict on GitLab user create but still resulted in a separate account.
- Hypothesis: SCIM mapping rules use different email fields for contractor vs employee and our GitLab connector creates unique accounts when email_normalized differs by alias.
- Risk: PATs and AWS keys could be used if contractor account remains active.

resolution: Partial remediation applied: contractor GitLab account disabled, contractor PATs revoked, AWS access key rotated. Courier scheduled for loaner pickup. Remaining: update SCIM mapping rules and add validation to prevent duplicate account creation; tracked as follow-up.
